def: A 16-bit floating-point format with fp32's 8 exponent bits and only 7 mantissa bits, giving fp32's range at lower precision and needing no loss scaling.
The IEEE 16-bit floating-point format with 5 exponent and 10 mantissa bits, more precise than bf16 but overflowing above 65,504.
The bits of a floating-point number that hold its significant digits and so set its precision.
The bits of a floating-point number that set its scale and so its range.
Multiplying the loss by a constant before the backward pass so that small fp16 gradients do not underflow to zero, then dividing the gradients by it before the update.
Adjusting the loss scale during training: halve it and skip the step when a gradient overflows, double it after a run of clean steps.
A full-precision fp32 copy of the weights that the optimiser updates, because tiny updates would be rounded away in 16-bit numbers.
Training with 16-bit numbers for the bulky matrix products and 32-bit numbers for accumulations such as weights, optimiser state and the loss.
A sudden large rise in training loss, common in long runs, from which the run may or may not recover.
Rescaling the gradient when its global norm exceeds a threshold, so that the direction is kept and the step length is capped.
The length of the gradient vector taken over all parameters, a leading indicator of instability when logged before clipping.
Raising the learning rate from near zero to its peak over the first steps of training, when the weights and the optimiser's statistics are least reliable.
Applying a normalisation to queries and keys before their dot product, which stops attention logits growing without bound.
An auxiliary loss on the log of the softmax denominator that keeps the output logits close to log-probabilities and helps stability.
